What SAX Is and Its Development Model

This page explains what SAX is, how a SAX UI project is put together, and the “pure UI, static placeholder data” development model. After reading it, you will be able to judge which scenarios suit SAX and understand the syntax, structure, and toolchain covered in the following pages.

What SAX Is

SAX is SA's UI dialect plugin (sa_plugin_sax), which compiles .sax source files into output that runs directly in the browser: app.wasm (component logic), airlock.js (the bridge between WASM and the DOM), index.html, and the intermediate product app.sa. Two companion plugins sit on top of SAX: sa_plugin_react provides a React-style way of writing code (className, event aliases, capitalized component composition, and so on), and sa_plugin_mui provides a Material component library published in SAX source form (mui/material.sax, mui/icons_material.sax).

NoteYour code is physically isolated from the JS/TS build chain: .sax → WASM goes through the SA toolchain the whole way, with no esbuild/tsc/node. The only JS in the browser is machine-generated glue (airlock.js and the dev hot-reload client), which never enters your source code.

The Pure-UI Project Model

The best-practice sample is D:\projects\sla\codex_ui: a pure-UI project that rebuilds a React UI with the SAX toolchain. Its boundary conventions:

  • UI only: it contains no real business logic; all data is static placeholder text (such as “CPU 23% · MEM 41%”, “12.4k in / 3.1k out”).
  • One independent .sax file per screen: the entry point is app.sax in the root directory, screens and region components live in screens/, and settings sections live in screens/settings/.
  • Cross-file components share one namespace: all files are passed to the compiler together via --include, and tags starting with a capital letter can reference each other.
  • All styling goes through global CSS classes (app.css); MUI library components use className plus child text/attributes to customize their appearance.
  • Interaction is only state switching: boolean state + fn handler() + render(), with no routing and no network requests.

The Development Navigation Bar: a Substitute for Multi-Screen Switching Gates

The state-machine gates / dialog switches of the original React application are replaced in SAX by a “development navigation bar” fixed at the bottom of the page (class name cxu-devnav). The entry component declares one i1 boolean state per screen; clicking a button sets the target screen to true, the rest to false, and calls render(); each screen is wrapped in a <section className="cxu-screen{nav_xxx ? '' : ' cxu-hidden'}">, and cxu-hidden (display:none) provides mutually exclusive display. The settings drawer uses the same technique internally for left-column switching among its 17 sections (the sec_xxx state family).

<Component name="CodexUiApp">
  <state>
    nav_workbench = 1 as i1
    nav_settings = 0 as i1
  </state>

  <div className="cxu-app">
    <section className="cxu-screen{nav_workbench ? '' : ' cxu-hidden'}">
      <WorkbenchScreen />
    </section>
    <section className="cxu-screen{nav_settings ? '' : ' cxu-hidden'}">
      <SettingsDrawerScreen />
    </section>
    <nav className="cxu-devnav">
      <button onClick={goto_workbench}>工作台</button>
      <button onClick={goto_settings}>设置</button>
    </nav>
  </div>

  fn goto_settings() {
    nav_workbench = false;
    nav_settings = true;
    render();
  }
</Component>
